text:
sam: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector change (prefer-affine-kernels=true) I'm seeing a reproducible perf regression + contention on pooled scratchpads. p50 gen latency +12ms, p99 +85ms, and two OOMs on a 12GB test node when running 8 concurrent 40-token chat lanes. Logs + quick repro below.

maya: @sam can you paste the nvprof / nvtx snippet? also which model & quantization?

sam: Model: open-7b-q4_0, runtime build: r2026.03.01. nvprof shows a lot of time stalled in small cudaMemcpyAsync + a sync on the eviction path when scratchpad freelist is exhausted. here's a trimmed chunk: ```
GPU: stalled 42% in memcpy, 30% in kernel launch overhead
Backtrace: scratchpad_eviction -> borrow_slab -> cudaMemcpyAsync(stream0) -> streamSynchronize somewhere in fallback path
```

devon: hmm that's consistent with what I saw when per-kernel affinity forced preferred kernels that use smaller per-op workspaces. If workspace < footprint of sticky logits buffer we end up evicting/rehydrating repeatedly. repeated evict/rehydrate => memcpy churn + cross-stream sync.

ara: Can you confirm whether logits buffers are being treated as ephemeral vs leased? Our old behavior was: logits = leased_per_request (fast path), scratchpad = pooled_shared. New kernel paths seem to treat logits as short-lived and allocate on scratchpad then free immediately which races with other lanes.

sam: Verified: allocator traces show logits allocations hitting the global slab freelist instead of per-stream freelist. There's a contention spike on the atomic freelist pop. Sample from allocator trace: ```
ALLOC logits 2.1MB -> slab-idx=11 -> atomic-pop stall=75us (avg)
FREE logits 2.1MB -> slab-idx=11 -> retire-queue length=32 -> force-evict path invoked
```

maya: OOM happened when retire-queue hit threshold and we triggered synchronous eviction which calls cudaStreamSynchronize on the caller stream. That sync is the p99 latency culprit.

devon: Proposed mitigations (short list):
- prefer per-stream freelists for logits/activation small-bufs (reduce atomics)
- lazy retire: move actual cudaFree/copy to background worker thread (epoch-based reclamation)
- warmup sticky logits for common seq lengths (avoid churn)
- fall back to coarser kernel affinity if workspace mismatch detected

ara: I prototyped an epoch-retire queue this morning. Sketch: ```
// simplified pseudo
void free_buf(buf) {
  buf->epoch = current_epoch.load();
  per_gpu.retire_queue.push(buf);
}
void background_reclaim() {
  while(true) {
    advance_epoch(); // after GPU idle checks / small sleep
    while(retire_queue.peek().epoch < safe_epoch) reclaim_one();
  }
}
```
This avoids immediate cudaFree/copy on hot path and batches frees to reduce syncs. latency improved in microbench by ~20% p99.

sam: Nice. Did you run with sticky logits warmup too?

ara: Yes — warmup + epoch-reclaim together removed the cross-stream sync and reduced allocator atomic wait from 75us -> 8us. Memory overhead ~ +3% during warmup windows.

maya: Can you share the perf numbers? we need concrete for canary decision.

sam: Run summary (8 lanes, 40 tokens each, 12GB GPU):
- baseline (pre-change): p50 72ms, p99 210ms, no OOMs
- after kernel-selector change (regression): p50 84ms, p99 295ms, 2x OOMs in 30min
- with per-stream freelist + epoch-reclaim + warmup: p50 74ms, p99 222ms, 0 OOMs
So mitigations mostly restore baseline and avoid OOM.

devon: That looks promising. Any downsides? retire queue + warmup increase resident set and complicates lifecycle. Also adds a background thread per-device which we need to coordinate at shutdown.

ara: Other edge cases: models with massive kv cache (long prefix use) still trigger eviction due to global cache pressure. The retire-queue helps but we should also avoid treating cached KV slices as scratchpad-eligible; mark them as "pinned" in allocator so they don't get evicted by the scratchpad reclaim path.

maya: Action items:
- ara: finish epoch-reclaim patch + unit tests (allocator invariants) — ETA 2d
- sam: add per-model config to mark pinned KV vs scratchpad-eligible and a canary config flag `allocator.epoch_reclaim=true` — ETA 1d
- devon: add a perf test to our CI harness that runs 8-lane 40-token shot and reports p50/p99 + OOMs — ETA 3d
- infra-bot: canary rollout to dedicated pool once flagged by devex (sam please request)

infra-bot: deploybot: canary job queued for pool "dedicated-test-a" with env `allocator.epoch_reclaim=true` — job id 98213

sam: I'll open the RFC/PR today with notes + nvprof traces attached. tagging @maya for observability dashboard tweaks (token-level cost/lock-time per-request).

maya: I'll add a per-route metric: scratchpad_contention_count and allocator_retire_queue_len to console. Also add NVTX hooks in the eviction path for easier flamegraphs.

devon: One more thought: kernel-selector should expose workspace-estimate API so runtime can ask "expected_workspace_for_seq(seq_len, model, kernel_variant)" before choosing an affinity. That would avoid picking a kernel that forces eviction mid-request. Worth an RFC if we want long-term correctness.

sam: Agreed. I'll add kernel workspace-estimate to the RFC. For now let's land epoch-reclaim + per-stream freelist canary and monitor. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
